look_mechanics:
# Living Grimoire gaze mechanics

The face is sculpted into a relatively rigid leather book cover, not a separate head. Preserve the readable canonical three-quarter cover and fixed left spine/right clasp. Do not rotate, mirror, skew or tilt the whole book to simulate gaze. The lower cream page block, four corners, forehead sun jewel, spine and clasp remain anchored with stable scale and baseline. Two attached ribbons stay compact and broadly resting; no pointing ribbon is needed to fake eye direction.

Natural motion: rotate the two physical cyan eye globes together inside their original sockets. The iris, pupil, highlight and visible sclera change as one coherent spherical surface; reshape eyelids and sculpted leather eyebrows to support the gaze. The soft facial leather immediately around the eyes and small mouth can subtly flex toward attention, without shifting the face outside its original cover footprint. No added eyes, overlay dots, detached pupils, new limbs, props or symbols. Keep the same large eye construction and eye spacing. The object construction makes a head turn unnatural; paired eye rotation plus lids/brows and very restrained cover-face relief supply direction instead.

Cardinal families in viewer coordinates:
- 000 up: both eye axes point conspicuously toward the top edge, pupils/irises high in sockets with sclera visibly below; brows lift, upper lids follow upward; small smile remains centered.
- 090 screen-right: both physical eyes rotate to the right edge with most sclera left of the irises; lids/brows follow right, soft facial relief subtly aims right. Book and clasp stay fixed.
- 180 down: both eyes aim conspicuously down with sclera above; upper lids lower and brows gently knit, mouth stays small; book remains fixed.
- 270 screen-left: both eyes rotate left with visible sclera on their right; lids/brows follow left and facial relief subtly aims left. Never mirror spine/clasp or book.

No cardinal should read neutral. Generate a continuous eye-gaze circle at evenly spaced 22.5-degree increments; keep large enough component on both axes for diagonals to remain legible. Near-cardinal diagonal cues may be subtle but must not reverse. Each neighboring step changes globe rotation and eyelid contour by similar amounts, with negligible hardware/ribbon displacement. Row9: up, up-right progressing to right, down-right progressing to down. Row10: down, down-left progressing to left, up-left progressing to up. Its final337.5 continues naturally into row9's000. Full ordered families must retain canonical book scale and lower-page baseline with clear blank gutters and all ribbon stars attached.
